title: Split config-directory resolution into a dual-root read side and a single-root write side, and add ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR as an alias that beats PI_CONFIG_DIR
one_line: Make ~/.omp and ~/.ultraworkers both readable by resolving the config root as an ordered candidate list, while every new write and the install-id's write path go only to the new root, and make the project-level .omp directory and the two Rust env readers exempt.
user_visible_effect: A user who upgrades mid-flight never loses their settings, sessions or install identity: an install that only has the old root keeps reading it, an install that has both prefers the new one, an install with neither falls back to the default, and everything newly written lands in the new root. Setting ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR wins over the legacy PI_CONFIG_DIR, and setting the wrong one of the two no longer silently points the user at an empty directory. Two things stay deliberately unchanged so the rename is not a history rewrite: a project-local .omp directory that is already committed to git keeps being read, and the native crash-log directory and the macOS OAuth recovery path keep honouring PI_CONFIG_DIR exactly as before.

files_touched.change: Add a legacy config-dir constant and an ordered candidate list; add getConfigDirCandidates() (pure, no I/O), getConfigReadRootName() (first-existing-then-cached), and getConfigWriteRootName() (always the new name). Rewire getConfigDirName() to the override-priority chain, getBaseConfigRoot() to the read root, and getInstallId() to read-then-write-new. Introduce a project-pinned constant for the project-level directory name. Add a cache-reset seam and call it from refreshDirsFromEnv(), setAgentDir() and setProfile() so the existing resolver-rebuild paths cannot leave a stale root behind. Extend the XDG appRoot resolution to cover both the new and the legacy spelling under both XDG categories.

steps.instruction: In packages/utils/src/dirs.ts, add a legacy config-dir constant next to CONFIG_DIR_NAME (line 27) holding the old ".omp" spelling, and an ordered candidate list constant with the new name first and the legacy name second. The ordering is the contract: canonical write target first, legacy-compatible fallback second, exactly the shape MAIN_CONFIG_FILENAMES at line 30 already models. Do not rename or repurpose CONFIG_DIR_NAME here — W6 owns flipping it, and flipping it in W4 is the mistake that makes W6 unreviewable.

Add getConfigDirCandidates(): string[] returning the ordered candidate list with no filesystem access and no caching. It must be the single source both the read and the write side derive from, so the two can never drift.

Add getConfigReadRootName(): resolve the first candidate that exists on disk under the home directory and cache the winner for the process lifetime; when no candidate exists, return the write root so a fresh install still gets a coherent default. Add a __resetConfigDirCacheForTests() reset seam following the naming already used by __resetInstallIdCacheForTests (dirs.ts:1153), __resetProfileSnapshotForTests and __resetDirsFromEnvForTests.

Add getConfigWriteRootName(): returns the new name unconditionally. It must not consult the filesystem, must not consult the cache, and must never return a legacy name. Every existing-writer path routes through it.
steps.anchor: packages/utils/src/dirs.ts, beside getConfigReadRootName added in step 3

steps.instruction: Rewire getConfigDirName() (currently `return process.env.PI_CONFIG_DIR || CONFIG_DIR_NAME;` at :298) to the explicit override-priority chain: ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR wins, then PI_CONFIG_DIR, then getConfigReadRootName(), then getConfigWriteRootName() as the default. Keep the existing fall-through-to-write-root behaviour so a fresh install with no directories at all still resolves to the new name.

Call __resetConfigDirCacheForTests() from refreshDirsFromEnv(), setAgentDir() and setProfile(). This is mandatory, not optional: those three functions already exist to rebuild the resolver after the environment changes, and a config-root cache that they do not clear is a cache that outlives the invalidation the module was designed around. Verified consequence if skipped — 8 test files assign process.env.PI_CONFIG_DIR at runtime and would read a frozen root: packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/pi-config-dir.test.ts, packages/coding-agent/test/profile-cli.test.ts, packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-session-isolation.test.ts, packages/stats/test/helpers/temp-agent.ts, packages/tui/test/keybindings-migration.test.ts, packages/utils/test/dirs-python-gateway.test.ts, packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts, packages/utils/test/profiles.test.ts.

Split getBaseConfigRoot() (dirs.ts:114-116) into a read variant and a write variant. The existing getBaseConfigRoot() name is load-bearing — packages/coding-agent/src/collab/registry.ts:167 and :29 import it, and getProfileConfigRoot at :119 derives from it — so keep the exported name resolving to the READ root and add an explicit write-root sibling. Do not silently repoint the existing export at the write root.

Rework getInstallId() (dirs.ts:1104-1150) to read from the ordered candidates and write to the write root. Read order: new root's install-id, then the legacy root's install-id. If a valid UUID is found at the legacy path, return that exact UUID and persist it to the new root so the next process reads it locally. Preserve everything the current implementation already gets right: the UUID_RE validity gate, the O_CREAT|O_EXCL create race with the loser re-reading the winner, the unlink-before-O_EXCL path for an unparseable file, and the in-memory fallback that keeps the id stable for the process when the write fails. A fresh UUID must never be minted while a readable legacy id exists.

Extend the XDG appRoot resolution at line 360 so it tries the new spelling and then the legacy spelling under each of XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME. The two layouts use DIFFERENT spellings and this is easy to get wrong: the home root is dot-prefixed (~/.omp) because it comes from CONFIG_DIR_NAME, while the XDG appRoot is bare ($XDG_DATA_HOME/omp) because line 360 joins APP_NAME. So the candidate set is ['ultraworkers','omp'] for XDG and ['.ultraworkers','.omp'] for home — do not share one list between them. Keep the existing named-profile pinning (the profilePath branch and its orphan-profile comment at :340-355) exactly as it is; that logic is deliberately narrow and W4 must not widen it.

In crates/pi-natives/src/crash_handler.rs, read ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR first and fall back to PI_CONFIG_DIR, preserving the existing `.filter(|s| !s.is_empty())` guard and the DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIR = ".omp" fallback at :49/:286/:344. Keep the JS-parity comment block at :48 and :293-296 accurate.

Write the three test files. Keep every one of them free of imports that transitively pull pi_natives — verified on this machine that a sibling importing the same @oh-my-pi/pi-utils/dirs entrypoint (packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts) reports 5 pass / 0 fail. Use explicit temp roots passed into the resolution path or per-test spyOn with vi.restoreAllMocks() in afterEach; never a long-lived process.env mutation, per AGENTS.md. Assert observable results — resolved paths, the returned UUID, the bytes on disk — never a literal string read back out of an implementation file.

code_shape:
Three new exported functions in packages/utils/src/dirs.ts, all reading from one ordered candidate list so read and write can never drift apart:

  export function getConfigDirCandidates(): string[]      // ordered [new, legacy], no I/O, no cache
  export function getConfigReadRootName(): string         // first candidate that exists under $HOME; cached; falls through to write root
  export function getConfigWriteRootName(): string        // always the new name; no fs, no cache, never a legacy name
  export function __resetConfigDirCacheForTests(): void   // reset seam, named after __resetInstallIdCacheForTests at :1153

Two spellings, NOT one list — the home root is dot-prefixed, the XDG appRoot is not:
  home:  ['.ultraworkers', '.omp']        // from CONFIG_DIR_NAME
  xdg:   ['ultraworkers',  'omp']         // from path.join(value, APP_NAME) at :360

getConfigDirName() (currently one line at :298) becomes the explicit precedence chain:
  ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR  >  PI_CONFIG_DIR  >  getConfigReadRootName()  >  getConfigWriteRootName()

getBaseConfigRoot() (:114) keeps its name and its READ semantics — it is imported by packages/coding-agent/src/collab/registry.ts:167 — and gains an explicit write-root sibling. getInstallId() (:1104) reads new-then-legacy and writes only to the write root, keeping UUID_RE validation, the O_CREAT|O_EXCL create race, the unlink-before-recreate path and the in-memory fallback intact.

A project-pinned constant (fixed at '.omp' for this milestone, per W6a option (b)) backs both getProjectAgentDir() (dirs.ts:589-591) and the four project-relative registry lookups in packages/coding-agent/src/discovery/helpers.ts (:1032, :1034, :1049, :1079).

Both Rust env readers gain the same new-beats-legacy precedence: crates/pi-natives/src/crash_handler.rs:269 and crates/pi-natives/src/oauth_callback/darwin.rs:441.

Module-load singletons that must call the cache reset: refreshDirsFromEnv() (:484), setAgentDir() (:502), setProfile() (:541). The existing `let dirs = new DirResolver({...})` at :449 is a fourth, import-time freeze.
test_contract:
Four contracts, each named for the failure a consumer would otherwise see.

(1) RESOLUTION ORDER — packages/utils/test/config-dir-dual-root.test.ts. Only the legacy root exists: config and session paths resolve beneath it. Both roots exist: the new root wins. Neither exists: the default (the new name) is used. Fails if the candidate list is reversed, if the legacy candidate is dropped, or if the no-root default silently falls back to the legacy name. A separate case pins the two-spelling XDG candidate set, because a shared list between the dot-prefixed home root and the bare XDG appRoot is wrong for exactly one of the two.

(2) INSTALL-ID CONTINUITY — packages/utils/test/install-id-legacy-read.test.ts. Plant a known UUID at the legacy install-id path, resolve with the new root present but empty, and assert the SAME UUID is returned and that the new root now holds it. This is a conversion assertion, not an existence assertion: the regression it catches is minting a fresh UUID, which is indistinguishable from a correct one at every call site. The only externally visible symptom of getting it wrong is a cost table that silently restarts — so this test is the entire defence.

(3) SPLIT READ/WRITE ROOT — packages/utils/test/config-dir-write-root.test.ts. With both roots existing, reads land on the legacy root while writes land on the new root. Fails if the read side is reused for writes, which is the precise condition that makes W6's acceptance criterion unreachable.

(4) OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE — packages/utils/test/config-dir-write-root.test.ts, its own test, not inferred from (1). PI_CONFIG_DIR to root A and ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR to root B resolves to B; drop the new one and it resolves to A; drop both and it falls through to the candidate list from (1). Silent failure if absent: mis-setting the two variables points a user's configuration at an empty directory with nothing printed anywhere.

Rules that apply to all four: no mock.module() (use spyOn on the imported module object, with vi.restoreAllMocks() in afterEach); no long-lived process.env mutation where an explicit root parameter or a per-test spy is available; no reading an implementation file and asserting on its text; assert resolved paths, returned UUIDs and on-disk bytes rather than echoed literals. The existing packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts must keep passing UNCHANGED — it pins current single-root behaviour, so it is the regression net for the resolver rewiring.

GATE DISCRIMINATION, PROVEN BY EXIT CODE — `bun test test/config-dir-dual-root.test.ts` against a not-yet-written file exits 1 ('The following filters did not match any test files'); `bun test ./test/install-id.test.ts` against a real passing file exits 0. The command therefore distinguishes 'not implemented' from 'implemented and passing', which is exactly the property that makes it usable as a red-able gate.
gate:
Run from the repo root.

  bun run check:ts
  cd packages/utils && bun test ./test/config-dir-dual-root.test.ts ./test/install-id-legacy-read.test.ts ./test/config-dir-write-root.test.ts
  cd ../.. && bun test ./packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts ./packages/utils/test/profiles.test.ts ./packages/utils/test/dirs-python-gateway.test.ts ./packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/pi-config-dir.test.ts

The leading './' on each path is required: without it Bun treats the argument as a name filter rather than a path, and the missing-file case still exits 1 but the real-file case reports '0 tests' in a way that is easy to misread as green.

RED-BEFORE-GREEN is mandatory for contract (2). Before the getInstallId() change, planting a UUID at the legacy install-id path and resolving with the new root empty returns a DIFFERENT freshly minted UUID, and the assertion that the planted value comes back fails. That is a true red, not a missing-file error, and it is the only proof that the change is doing anything.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, so a vacuous green is impossible: before trusting the suite, confirm each new file reports a non-zero pass count. A file that loads and reports '0 pass' has asserted nothing. The missing-file control above (exit 1) plus a deliberate temporary break in getConfigWriteRootName() (return the legacy name, expect contract 3 and contract 4 to go red) together establish that these tests can actually fail.

REGRESSION NET: packages/utils/test/install-id.test.ts must pass UNCHANGED — it pins the current single-root install-id behaviour, so it is what proves the resolver rewiring did not disturb an unrelated contract.

CROSS-PACKAGE, NO NEW AUTOMATED GATE: `bun test ./packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/pi-config-dir.test.ts` covers the helpers.ts rewiring on the TypeScript side. The two Rust files have no test harness in this milestone — `bun run check:rs` type-checks them, and the darwin.rs path in particular is macOS-only, so a reviewer must read those two hunks rather than rely on a run. Say so in the PR rather than implying a green run covered them.
gate_can_fail:
Yes, in five ways that were each verified against the real tree rather than assumed.

(a) Mint instead of read. If getInstallId() falls through to generating a new UUID when only the legacy path is readable, contract (2) goes red. Verified that this is a TRUE red rather than an environment problem: the probe above shows the read accessor is live, so a planted legacy file really is found by the test. This is the single failure that silently costs money — a new UUID is indistinguishable from a correct one at every call site, and the only symptom is a cost table restarting.

(b) Do not clear the cache. If refreshDirsFromEnv() (:484), setAgentDir() (:502) and setProfile() (:541) do not call the new reset, the eight test files that assign process.env.PI_CONFIG_DIR at runtime read a frozen root and go red. Verified list in step 6. This is the failure mode that would make the change look correct in a fresh single-test run and break the wider suite — precisely why the third gate command includes packages/utils/test/profiles.test.ts and packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/pi-config-dir.test.ts.

(c) Leave the project path on the home accessor. If helpers.ts:1032/:1034/:1049/:1079 still call getConfigDirName(), every project with a committed .omp stops resolving its installed_plugins.json the moment the new root wins. Note the failure is deferred: at W4 the new root is never created, so this passes today and breaks at W5/W6. The negative control in the gate (deliberately flipping getConfigWriteRootName to the legacy name) is what surfaces it inside W4 rather than three items later.

(d) Share one candidate list between the home and XDG spellings. The home root is dot-prefixed, the XDG appRoot is not (dirs.ts:360 joins APP_NAME). One shared list is wrong for exactly one of the two, and the wrong one is invisible on a machine without XDG_*_HOME set — which is most CI.

(e) Extend the alias to TypeScript only. The crash-log directory (crash_handler.rs:269) and the macOS OAuth recovery path (darwin.rs:441) would keep honouring PI_CONFIG_DIR alone, so a user who sets only ULTRAWORKERS_CONFIG_DIR gets a coherent config root and an incoherent crash-log directory. No test in the repo catches this; only reading the two hunks does.

Separately: the brief's claim that `bun test` is blocked on this machine is FALSE and must not be propagated. It reports 5 pass / 0 fail for install-id.test.ts and 2 pass / 0 fail for dirs-python-gateway.test.ts; the 17 failures in the full packages/utils run are the pi_natives addon and are confined to logger-contract.test.ts and procmgr.test.ts. `bun run check:ts` exits 0. The real limitation is that `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build` fails without ninja, which only matters if a change here needs the native addon rebuilt — and none of the four files W4 touches do.

effort: M. The candidate list itself is small — roughly 40 lines across one module. What makes it M rather than S is that three separate mechanisms each have their own way of failing quietly: splitting install-id read from write while keeping UUID validation and the O_EXCL create race intact; adding a cache to an accessor that the module already freezes in four different places; and keeping the project-level and Rust paths off the home-side name. The plan calls this M and that rating holds.
risk:
The dominant risk is a failure that produces no error, no warning, and no failing test at the moment it ships. Three of them qualify. (1) A freshly minted install-id is indistinguishable from a correct one at every call site; the only symptom is a cost table that silently restarts. (2) Getting the two override variables backwards points a user at an empty configuration directory with nothing printed — which is why contract (4) is a separate test rather than an inference. (3) Leaving the project-level .omp on the home accessor is invisible at W4 (the new root does not exist yet) and detonates at W5/W6, so it is a bug that would be attributed to the wrong commit.

The second-order risk is over-reach: W6 owns flipping CONFIG_DIR_NAME and W5 owns the migration command. If W4 flips CONFIG_DIR_NAME 'just to be sure', W6 stops being a one-line revert and the milestone loses its safety property. If W4 starts moving directories, it duplicates W5 and its dry-run-by-default guarantee with it.

The third is platform-split blindness. darwin.rs is macOS-only and XDG candidate resolution is invisible without XDG_*_HOME set, so a single CI platform will not exercise either. Neither may be left to a reviewer's memory.

Mitigation is mostly the gate: a red-before-green assertion for install-id, a negative control proving the suite can fail, and unchanged-pass on the pre-existing install-id test as the regression net.
open_questions: Should getConfigDirCandidates() include the project-level name, or stay strictly home-scoped? This spec keeps it home-scoped and gives the project path its own pinned constant, matching W6a option (b). If the product later wants a project-level dual root too, that is W6a option (a) and it additionally requires config migrate to move project .omp directories — which are often committed to git, so migrate would have to read both and never delete.

The plan's M5 open question on the PI_*/OMP_* family (plan line 14025) is answered 'keep forever as aliases' by N16, and W4 implements exactly that for one variable. The other 149 runtime-read names in the family stay PI_-prefixed in this milestone. Confirm that is intended rather than an oversight, since the product will ship named ultraworkers with PI_-prefixed configuration vocabulary.

docs/environment-variables.md documents 100 env variables. W4 adds one row and amends one. Should the other config-adjacent variables in the family get new aliases in a later wave, or is one alias sufficient evidence of the pattern?

Should the cache be process-lifetime, or should config migrate be able to force a re-resolution in-process? With a process-lifetime cache, a migrate that moves ~/.omp to ~/.ultraworkers leaves the running process resolving to a directory that no longer exists. That is harmless for a one-shot CLI command that exits, but it should be a stated decision rather than an accident.
